primary_question: How much can combined electromagnetic design and fault-tolerant control increase actuator tolerance to conducted and near-field EMI?
alignment: Aligned; receiver characterization remains the critical path. EDMD is a separate supporting estimation workstream.

fresh_verification.result_source: Coordinator-confirmed main, hybrid, Python and reproduction results; this reviewer independently ran the original SC01B tests and rechecked frozen hashes.
fresh_verification.broad_campaign_reproduction_scope: Completed for 116 legacy controller records, 16 four-way development records, 24 four-way native comparisons, 16 native refinements and the full hybrid EDMD study. The original SC01B native/SPICE campaign was not rerun; other historical campaigns beyond the listed scope were not reproduced in this review.

fresh_reproduction.legacy_equality: Exact isequaln comparison, including matching NaN masks; no tolerance.
fresh_reproduction.native_comparison_scope: Four-way receiver study; numerical agreement does not establish physical validity outside the receiver domain.
fresh_reproduction.original_sc01b_test_scope: 22 isolated original-scope analytic metrics, energy accounting and output-preservation tests; no R2 path or native/SPICE campaign.

goals.supported: Nominal three-state model, controller, matched no-fault runs, freshly reproduced 116 legacy records with all 31 channels, plant traces and reason fields exact, and newly passed regression suite.
goals.remaining: Physical actuator/load identification; numerical reproduction does not establish hardware behavior.

goals.supported: Capacitive, inductive and shared-impedance equations, sensitivity studies and circuit comparisons; integrated capacitive A channel.
goals.remaining: Defensible receiver domain and measured cable/return/mutual behavior; ideal B timing limits the integrated scope.

goals.objective: Repeatable sensor, power and communication fault injection
goals.supported: Encoder, timestamped communication, ground-offset and averaged motor-bus mechanisms.
goals.remaining: Current-sensor corruption, physical controller brownout and full protocol-specific physical errors.

goals.objective: Fault detection using physical limits and model residuals
goals.supported: Plausibility, residual and freshness checks with saved missed-fault outcomes.
goals.remaining: Stationary freeze, small bias, slow drift, model/load uncertainty and calibrated thresholds. EDMD does not close these gaps.

goals.objective: Degraded operation, recovery and safe-stop logic
goals.supported: Numerical supervision, qualification/reset, optional reference reconstruction, motion shaping and separate stop/hold study.
goals.remaining: Failed primary-only recovery, motion under zero-voltage load, integrated drive/brake handoff and reliable loaded restart.

goals.supported: Causal interface, freshly reproduced 16 development records and eight clean companions, with unchanged rejection outcomes and evaluation still blocked.
goals.remaining: Usable receiver model, accepted development, newly frozen comparison and complete evaluation.

development_outcomes.DEV01: No persistent EMI count corruption or paired actuator disturbance.
development_outcomes.DEV02: All four exposed arms exceed the assumed 7 V receiver domain.

goals.supported: Source history, provenance, reproduction instructions and reports; fresh four-way native numerical comparisons passed 24/24 and refinements passed 16/16.
goals.remaining: Twelve native operating points remain outside the receiver domain; selected hardware, connected schematic, calibration, independent measurements and partial literature review.

edmd.recommendation: Keep separate from the control path and the receiver milestone; compare a small linear correction with a disturbance-estimating physics observer.

priorities: Preserve the newly passed software checks, scoped reproductions and all 16 frozen-file hashes; keep receiver-domain rejections visible and the readable plan separate from the authoritative restored source.
Complete receiver/topology assumptions and electrical characterization before control-effect scoring.
Freeze new separate development/evaluation fixtures, then compare the four arms only after acceptance.
Keep loaded restart, remaining physical fault mechanisms and literature work tied to their specific claims.
Maintain EDMD as documented supporting work with its negative quadratic-versus-linear result and unchanged Draft approvals.
